rows.description: Demands for donations, unpaid labour, cutting off family, or secrecy are signs of exploitation. It is not your foolishness; these groups target sincere seekers. Step back, consult trusted family, and seek outside counsel.

related mind states: trust

rows.description: The satsang feels like a family that finally accepts you. Enjoy it, and also keep outside friendships and questions alive. A healthy community allows you to leave, disagree and still be respected.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, disillusionment, exploitation, fear, protectiveness, worship
related mind states: admiration, nostalgia

rows.description: Members guilt you for missing events, hint at karma or punishment, or watch your choices. This is control, not care. Set small boundaries, spend time with outsiders, and know you can leave without shame.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, disillusionment, exploitation, fear, protectiveness, worship
related mind states: shame, guilt

rows.description: You discover the teacher lives differently from what they preach or hides wrongdoing. Grief and anger are natural. Separate the good you learned from the person, report abuse, and do not conclude that all sincerity is fake.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, coercion, exploitation, fear, protectiveness, worship
related mind states: grief, anger

rows.description: Your family fears you are being drawn into a cult and reacts with ridicule or force. Listen to specific concerns, stay in contact, and invite them to meet the community. Isolation grows when both sides harden.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, coercion, disillusionment, exploitation, protectiveness, worship
related mind states: fear, anxiety, loneliness

rows.description: A friend is giving all savings and time to a group, and you worry. Stay warm, ask open questions, and do not attack their belief. Keeping the friendship alive is what lets them turn to you when doubts rise.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, coercion, disillusionment, exploitation, fear, worship
related mind states: anxiety, doubt

rows.description: You search for meaning after burnout or loss and try many paths. Seeking is honest and human. Go slowly, test teachings against daily life, avoid promises of instant enlightenment, and keep questioning.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, coercion, disillusionment, exploitation, fear, protectiveness

rows.description: A relative or colleague praises a leader you distrust, and heat rises. Mature action: ask what worries them, find shared facts, and disengage when it turns to insults. Winning the argument seldom changes a mind or protects a relationship.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, admiration, argument, contempt, loyalty
related mind states: anger, anxiety, interest

rows.description: You think the other side is stupid or evil. Contempt feels superior but blinds you to real grievances and persuades no one. Try to explain their strongest view before disagreeing; that keeps you honest and humane.

rows.description: Being dismissed as brainwashed or anti-national stings and closes you. You can end a conversation calmly, state your view briefly, and refuse to be defined by a label. Dignity does not require winning the exchange.
